newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie says Q1 ahead of year ago.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie says Q1 ahead of year ago.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Wednesday its results for its first quarter to end-June were well ahead of last year.
Macquarie Bank said also it was unlikely to take any action that would lead to a major reduction in capital.
"First quarter results are well ahead of the comparable period last year," Macquarie Bank executive chairman David Clarke told the annual meeting.
Favourable market conditions for the treasury, commodities and equities groups were a major factor contributing to the first quarter results.

Clarke said the Reserve Bank's new capital adequacy standards for capital risk to apply from January 1, 1998 would increase Macquarie's capital adequacy ratio to about 16 percent, with a tier one capital ratio of about 13 percent.
"We recognise that a tier one capital adequacy ratio of 13 percent has been a topic of investor discussion in recent time," he said.
"It is unlikely that any action will involve a major reduction in our capital," he said.
"We are analysing the situation and will communicate with shareholders later in the year," he said.

Newspaper have reported in recent days that Macquarie was considering a share buy-back or other form of capital returns to absorb A$150 million of excess capital and reduce its tier one capital adequacy ratio to about nine percent.

Clarke said Macquarie's project and structured finance division had had a successful start to the year with its involvement in the Loy Yang A power privatisation and its selection as preferred developer along with Lend Lease Corp for the underground rail link to Bondi beach in Sydney.
He said the recent decline in the gold price had increased trading activity for the short term at least.
"However, a sustained price decline is likely to result in a reduction of producer hedging business as development of new projects is more critically assessed," he said.
Clarke said Macquarie did not expect its PUMA mortgage securitisation arm to produce a significant increase in profit contribution for the current year.
Macquarie Bank reported a net profit of A$116.94 million for the year to March 31, up from A$93.2 million the previous year.
